If the two valuations in the minimum are unequal, equality holds. Legendre's formula counts multiples of p, p^2, and so on inside a factorial:

items.text: The valuation base p must be prime for these divisibility laws in this form.
The factorial sum is finite because all later floor terms are zero.
For a quotient of integers, subtract denominator valuations only when the quotient is interpreted as a nonzero rational number.
The valuation of a sum can exceed the minimum when the lowest-power terms cancel.

examples.title: Find the power of 2 dividing a factorial

items.text: Do not stop Legendre's sum after floor(n/p); multiples of p^2 contribute extra copies.
Do not replace the valuation-of-a-sum inequality by equality without checking for cancellation.
The infinity convention for zero is useful algebraically but must not be treated as an ordinary integer exponent.
